introduction:
Introduction About TORITZ 100MG INJECTION

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION contains Rituximab which belongs to the group of medicines called Anticancer drugs. It is used to manage blood cancer (leukaemia) and lymph cancer (lymphoma). It can also be used to manage various auto-immune disease conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis (inflammation of blood vessels) and pemphigus vulgaris (severe skin blistering and peeling especially on the mouth, nose, throat, eyes and genitals).

It is mostly used in combination with other cytotoxic anticancer agents to achieve better results. It is suitable for use both in adults and in children (aged 6 months or older). TORITZ 100MG INJECTION will be administered to you only by an oncologist or a trained professional into your vein (as intravenous infusion).

Before receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION inform your doctor if you have any heart problems (such as chest pain, heart attack, heart failure or abnormal heartbeat). You must also inform your doctor if you currently have or previously had hepatitis B infection or any other mild infections (including minor cough and cold) as a precaution.

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION is not recommended for use in pregnant or breastfeeding women. Both men and women receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION must use a suitable contraceptive method to avoid pregnancy while undergoing therapy with TORITZ 100MG INJECTION.

The most common side effects of receiving this medicine are fever, chills, skin rashes with itching, shortness of breath and low blood pressure. Consult your doctor if any of these side effect worsens.

usesDetails:
Uses Of TORITZ 100MG INJECTION

It is used to manage:

Blood cancer (Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia)
Lymph cancer (Non-Hodgkin’s Lymphoma)
Rheumatoid arthritis (joint pain and inflammation)
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis (inflammation of blood vessels)
Pemphigus vulgaris (severe skin blistering and peeling especially on the mouth, nose, throat, eyes and genitals)
mechanismOfAction:
How TORITZ 100MG INJECTION Works

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION is a monoclonal antibody. It destroys the immune cells (B-cells) that triggers cancer formation. It also reduces the production of certain chemicals within the body (such as rheumatoid factor, T-cells, cytokines) that causes inflammation, pain and swelling which helps in managing various autoimmune diseases.
usageDetails:
How to use TORITZ 100MG INJECTION

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION will be given to you only by a doctor or a nurse into the vein (intravenously).

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition.

warnings.details: TORITZ 100MG INJECTION is generally not recommended for use in pregnant women. However, consult your doctor before receiving it. Women of childbearing potential must use a suitable contraceptive to avoid pregnancy while undergoing therapy with TORITZ 100MG INJECTION and until 12 months after stopping the therapy. If you accidentally became pregnant while receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION, inform your doctor immediately.
TORITZ 100MG INJECTION is not recommended for use in breastfeeding women. Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.
Do not drive or operate any machines if your ability is affected by TORITZ 100MG INJECTION.
Avoid consumption of alcohol while receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION as it may make you feel drowsier.
Talk to your doctor before receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION if you are allergic to rituximab.

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION is not recommended for use in patients with severe heart failure or uncontrollable heart problems. It should be used with caution in patients with other heart problems (such as angina, fast heart rate or heart failure). Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

Others

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION is not recommended for use if you:

Have any serious infection that affects the whole body
Have a weak immune system

Before receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you:

Currently have or previously had hepatitis B infection
Are yet to receive any vaccinations
Have any infection (including mild cough and cold)
Have a previous history of severe infections

Use in pediatrics:

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION should be used in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years) only if prescribed by the physician. Therefore, consult your doctor for advice before receiving it.

Use in geriatrics:

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years or above). Therefore, consult your doctor before receiving it.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before receiving TORITZ 100MG INJECTION, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines such as:

Medicines used to manage high blood pressure (such as atenolol, propranolol, amlodipine, enalapril, olmesartan, losartan)
Medicines that can suppress immune functions (such as ciclosporin, tacrolimus)
Other anticancer medicines (such as Trastuzumab, Bevacizumab, Alemtuzumab, Cetuximab)

Overdosage:

TORITZ 100MG INJECTION will be administered to you only by a doctor or a nurse in a hospital, and so it is unlikely to receive an overdose. However, consult your doctor if you experience any unusual symptoms.
